title: A listener registry that never breaks mid-event

blocks.text: A listener registry is read on every event and written only when a listener joins or leaves: the read-heavy, write-rare work `CopyOnWriteArrayList` is made for. Its iterator walks the array that was current when the iterator was created, so it never throws `ConcurrentModificationException`, and it never sees a write made after it started. The page's example:

Write `EventBus<E>` with `subscribe(Consumer<E>)`, `unsubscribe(Consumer<E>)` and `publish(E event)`, which hands the event to every subscribed listener in the order they subscribed. A listener may subscribe or unsubscribe listeners, itself included, while it is handling an event, and then:

items: **nothing throws**: a listener that subscribes another during `publish` breaks nothing;

**an event in flight goes to the listeners subscribed when its `publish` began**: a listener subscribed during `publish` gets only later events, and a listener that leaves during `publish`, or is removed by another listener during it, still gets that event and no later one; no other listener misses it;
**each `subscribe` is one subscription**: a listener subscribed twice hears each event twice, and one `unsubscribe` removes one of its subscriptions.

blocks.text: The tests grade what one thread shows: publishing while listeners join and leave. Many threads publishing and subscribing at once is why the page picks `CopyOnWriteArrayList`, and it is not graded.

cases.says: Two listeners hear x and y in subscription order; an unsubscribed one hears nothing.
A listener that subscribes another while handling x makes neither publish throw.
A listener subscribed while x is being published hears y, not x.
A listener that unsubscribes itself while handling x does not make b or c miss x.
A listener subscribed twice hears each event twice; unsubscribing it once removes one subscription, so it then hears each event once.

concepts: CopyOnWriteArrayList suits read-heavy, write-rare work such as a listener registry.
A CopyOnWriteArrayList iterator reads the array captured when it was created, so it never throws and never sees a later write.
